purpose: Requirements for accepting inbound JWTs from a configured header or cookie on the Codex endpoint.

requirements.statement: accept an optional [server.auth] jwt_header key naming a request header from which an inbound JWT is read, stripping a leading Bearer scheme when present

scenarios.name: When a Codex request to /v1/responses carries a valid identity-provider JWT in the header named by jwt_header and no Authorization header, the system shall authenticate the caller and serve the turn.
when: a Codex request to /v1/responses carries a valid identity-provider JWT in that header and no Authorization header
then: the system authenticates the caller and serves the turn

scenarios.name: When the configured header's value is Bearer <jwt>, the system shall verify <jwt> without the scheme prefix.
when: the configured header's value is Bearer <jwt>
then: the system verifies <jwt> without the scheme prefix

scenarios.name: If a request carries the configured header more than once and no earlier slot authenticates the caller, then the system shall reject the request with 401.
given: no earlier slot authenticates the caller
when: a request carries the configured header more than once
then: the system rejects the request with 401

requirements.statement: accept an optional [server.auth] jwt_cookie key naming a cookie from which an inbound JWT is read

scenarios.name: When a Codex WebSocket upgrade on /backend-api/codex/responses carries a valid JWT in the cookie named by jwt_cookie among other cookies, the system shall authenticate the upgrade before switching protocols.
when: a Codex WebSocket upgrade on /backend-api/codex/responses carries a valid JWT in that cookie among other cookies
then: the system authenticates the upgrade before switching protocols

scenarios.name: If a request carries the configured cookie name more than once, counted across every cookie header field, and no earlier slot authenticates the caller, then the system shall reject the request with 401.
given: no earlier slot authenticates the caller
when: a request carries the configured cookie name more than once across its cookie header fields
then: the system rejects the request with 401

requirements.statement: verify a token found in a configured header or cookie against the configured [[server.auth.jwt]] entries with exactly the rules applied to a bearer JWT (issuer, audience, authorized party, token age, claim rules, identity claim)

scenarios.name: If the token in the configured header was issued for a different audience, then the system shall reject the request with 401.
when: the token in the configured header was issued for a different audience
then: the system rejects the request with 401

requirements.statement: read the configured header and cookie on the inbound Codex endpoint's routes only — Responses over HTTP and WebSocket on all three base paths, web search, and the client analytics sink — and nowhere else

scenarios.name: When a Codex request to /v1/responses carries a valid identity-provider JWT in the header named by jwt_header and no Authorization header, the system shall authenticate the caller and serve the turn.
when: a Codex request to /v1/responses carries a valid identity-provider JWT in that header and no Authorization header
then: the system authenticates the caller and serves the turn

scenarios.name: When a Codex WebSocket upgrade on /backend-api/codex/responses carries a valid JWT in the cookie named by jwt_cookie among other cookies, the system shall authenticate the upgrade before switching protocols.
when: a Codex WebSocket upgrade on /backend-api/codex/responses carries a valid JWT in that cookie among other cookies
then: the system authenticates the upgrade before switching protocols

scenarios.name: When a request to /v1/messages carries a valid JWT only in the configured header or cookie, the system shall reject it as unauthenticated.
when: a request to /v1/messages carries a valid JWT only in the configured header or cookie
then: the system rejects it as unauthenticated

requirements.statement: try the credential slots in a fixed order — static token, then Authorization: Bearer JWT, then the configured header, then the configured cookie — and authenticate the caller with the first slot that succeeds

scenarios.name: When Authorization carries a ChatGPT sign-in token from an issuer no [[server.auth.jwt]] entry names and the configured cookie carries a valid JWT, the system shall authenticate the caller from the cookie.
when: Authorization carries a ChatGPT sign-in token from an unconfigured issuer and the configured cookie carries a valid JWT
then: the system authenticates the caller from the cookie

requirements.statement: use the verified identity from a header or cookie token as the caller principal for usage attribution, spend limits, and account-pool session stickiness, exactly as a bearer JWT identity is used

scenarios.name: When a caller authenticated from the configured cookie is over its spend cap, the system shall refuse the turn with usage_limit_reached under that caller's identity.
given: the caller authenticated from the configured cookie is over its spend cap
then: the system refuses the turn with usage_limit_reached under that caller's identity

requirements.statement: remove the configured header and every cookie header from the request before it is forwarded to any upstream, on both HTTP and WebSocket

scenarios.name: When a request authenticated from the configured header is forwarded to the ChatGPT/Codex account pool, the upstream request shall contain neither the configured header nor any cookie header.
when: a request authenticated from the configured header is forwarded to the ChatGPT/Codex account pool
then: the upstream request contains neither the configured header nor any cookie header

scenarios.name: When a Codex request is served by a [[server.codex_endpoint.routes]] route to a non-ChatGPT upstream, the upstream request shall contain neither the configured header nor any cookie header.
when: a Codex request is served by a [[server.codex_endpoint.routes]] route to a non-ChatGPT upstream
then: the upstream request contains neither the configured header nor any cookie header

requirements.statement: reject at startup a configuration that sets jwt_header or jwt_cookie without any [[server.auth.jwt]] entry, a jwt_header that is not a valid header name, equals (case-insensitively) authorization, x-api-key, cookie, a shunt-reserved header name, a header shunt itself reads or rewrites on the Codex endpoint (session-id, x-claude-code-session-id, content-type, content-length, content-encoding, transfer-encoding, host, origin, upgrade, connection, openai-beta, sec-websocket-*) or that the Codex CLI sends or shunt synthesizes there (originator, x-codex-routing-hint, thread-id, x-client-request-id, x-codex-window-id), or the [server.auth] or [server.admin] header name, and a jwt_cookie that is empty, not a valid cookie name, or equal (case-insensitively) to the admin dashboard's shunt_admin_session cookie

scenarios.name: If jwt_cookie is set and no [[server.auth.jwt]] entry exists, then the system shall refuse to start and name the offending key.
then: the system refuses to start and names the offending key

scenarios.name: If jwt_header equals the [server.admin] header name, then the system shall refuse to start.

requirements.statement: keep gateway-owned authentication failures on the Codex endpoint in the OpenAI Responses error shape and status codes — one undifferentiated 401 for a missing or rejected credential, 503 when no slot authenticates and at least one presented token names a configured issuer whose key set cannot be fetched

scenarios.name: If the configured header carries a token from a configured issuer whose key set cannot be fetched and no other slot authenticates, then the system shall respond 503 in the OpenAI Responses error shape.
when: the configured header carries a token from a configured issuer whose key set cannot be fetched
then: the system responds 503 in the OpenAI Responses error shape

requirements.statement: apply configuration reloads to jwt_header and jwt_cookie the same way reloads already apply to [server.auth]

scenarios.name: When a reload adds jwt_header to a running configuration, the system shall accept a JWT from that header on the next Codex request without a restart.
then: the system accepts a JWT from that header on the next Codex request without a restart

requirements.statement: consult the configured cookie only when the request carries no Origin header or one whose origin matches the request's scheme (X-Forwarded-Proto, else http), Host, and effective port

scenarios.name: If a WebSocket upgrade carries a valid JWT only in the configured cookie and an Origin whose host differs from the request's Host, then the system shall reject the upgrade with 401.
when: a WebSocket upgrade carries a valid JWT only in the configured cookie and an Origin whose host differs from the request's Host
then: the system rejects the upgrade with 401

requirements.statement: leave behavior unchanged for every deployment that sets neither jwt_header nor jwt_cookie — same accepted credentials, same headers forwarded, same responses
avoid disclosing which credential slot or which check failed in an authentication error or in logs at default verbosity, and never log a token value
